newsitem.title: USA: Orange Cty agency sues KPMG over investment losses.
newsitem.headline: Orange Cty agency sues KPMG over investment losses.

text.p: Orange County, Calif., Transportation Authority has sued KPMG Peat Marwick LLP for at least $400 million for allegedly not warning it about the risks in the county's investment portfolio.

Transit authority spokesman John Standiford said the lawsuit, filed last week in Orange County Superior Court, alleged that auditor KPMG Peat Marwick misrepresented the liquidity of the assets in the ill-fated county portfolio.
KPMG Peat Marwick has maintained that it acted properly. "We were not the county's investment advisers and we've done nothing wrong," a spokesman for the firm said Thursday.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June.
Last December, Orange County sued KPMG Peat Marwick, seeking as much as $3 billion. The county accused its former auditor of breach of contract and professional negligence.

The Orange County Transportation Authority, which provides bus and other transportation services and funds local freeway construction, said it had deposited about $1 billion in the county portfolio. The authority said it lost more than $225 million when the county's investments crashed in 1994.
The authority said it had retained KPMG Peat Marwick to audit its finances between 1991 and 1994.
The suit alleged that the firm knew or "should have known" in the months before the bankruptcy that the "problems in the pool were so severe that the pool was in effect insolvent," Standiford said.
Instead, the authority alleged that KPMG Peat Marwick maintained that the investments were "safe and liquid."
